3.name: Baile ghorm

4.name: Baile dhubh

5.name: Doire mhin

6.name: Cuan bheag

8.name: Dùn thais

9.name: Inis mhin

10.name: Cuan dhearg

11.name: Cnoc ghlas

12.name: Àth fhiadhaich
12.why: Shire seat and river-mouth harbour of the eastern road; its Seann Spioradan house refused to bless the copper (V). Port cleared: its map cell lies inland (distance 6 from the coast) with no haven; it keeps its river.

20.why: Shire seat and grain port; first and richest Hawk house (B_faiths); barracks of An siathamh rèisimeid; faces the Tuathaich border. Port cleared: its map cell lies inland (distance 5 from the coast) with no haven; it keeps its river.

21.name: Cnoc bhàn

22.name: Ceann leathan

Its port is kept on the lake: the town was moved 3 cells to the lake shore (see burg_moves.json).

28.why: Hill pasture village by an old cairn; nothing to add.

38.name: Cuan bheag

444.why: 'Walled to collect tolls rather than to keep enemies out', and still collects them.

445.name: Àth dhearg
445.why: Tuathaich ford under the Baile chrom light.

446.name: Baile shean
446.why: Old quay. Its port is kept: the town was moved 1 cell to the coast (see burg_moves.json).

447.name: Àth fhionn
447.why: Small human waystation kept by the Tuathaich.

448.name: Àth ghlas
448.why: Grey ford that replaced the old bridge.

449.name: Achadh chaol
449.why: Shire seat of barley fields; its people went to the pits elsewhere in the drought (IV).

450.name: Ceann òg
450.why: 'Built as a trading quay in the first years after the Crossing'. Port cleared: its map cell lies inland (distance 7 from the coast) with no haven; it keeps its river.

453.name: Achadh mhòr
453.why: Border fields trading with both sides.

455.name: Muileann àrsaidh
455.why: Ancient mill fortified with a citadel (group fort).

456.name: Cnoc uaine
456.why: Founded by keepers of the holy wood, on its edge.

458.name: Muileann dhearg
458.why: Walled mill town, walled in the Age of Strangers.

459.name: Cnoc òg
459.why: Bakers and harness-makers supplying the Inis mhòr garrison.

460.name: Baile bhàn
460.why: Citadel built to guard the church-town of Cill dhìreach and its treasuries.

461.name: Cill dhìreach
461.why: Shire seat; 'a church village of twenty-four thousand' whose priests tend the melee's wounded; the pit crews' first-coal shrine (IV).

462.name: Cnoc dhìreach
462.why: Shire seat; 'walled seat of the eastern mining district', walled during the strikes of the Age of Strangers.

466.name: Muileann dhomhain
466.why: Shire seat of the deep mill-pools; the swallowing cough (III).

468.name: Cill chaol
468.why: Dia-thìrich chapel village whose chapel the Tuathaich turned to the worship of Donn.

470.name: Baile dhubh
470.why: 'Built by human colliers in the Age of Strangers on one of the northern coal seams'; coal pits of the northern holdouts.

471.name: Dùn dhubh
471.why: 'A walled hill fort of dark stone', raised in the Holy Age and repaired in every age.

473.name: Cnoc dhubh
473.why: Coal seams dug by the humans and kept open by the Tuathaich; 'the last coal pits of the north'.

475.name: Caol bheag
475.why: Shire seat; harbour town of forty thousand crowned by a citadel; the fourth regiment's station; the largest town of the Deer. Port cleared: its map cell lies inland (distance 4 from the coast) with no haven; it keeps its river.

476.name: Cathair gheal
476.why: Walled city of white stone; the human concession's market town with a magistrate's hall and a chapel, which shut its gates in the war (IV).

477.name: Muileann bheag
477.why: Mills for Inis mhòr and Caol bheag.

478.name: Àth bheag
478.why: A ford settled by Tuathaich families sent north at the Severance.

479.name: Baile dhomhain
479.why: Walled Hawk town, walls raised in the Age of Strangers and strengthened after the Severance.

481.name: Baile dhìreach
481.why: Trades over the line; nothing more.

482.name: Cnoc gheal
482.why: 'A white hill with a shrine of the Yellow Scorpion'.

483.name: Achadh ghlas
483.why: Fields that quartered soldiers in the war.

484.name: Baile Mòr àrsaidh
484.why: 'An ancient market city of the northern plain'.

488.name: Cill gharbh
488.why: 'A village around a rough stone chapel' older than its houses.

489.name: Seann Skell
489.why: Shire seat and the largest town, seat of the Scorpion with its synod and harbour priests; 'walled by its citadel rather than by curtain walls'; seventh regiment; enforcers posted to close the western pits (V). Port cleared: its map cell lies inland (distance 6 from the coast) with no haven; it keeps its river.

491.name: Muileann dhearg
491.why: Shire seat by Cill ghlas; the vein-house above it (III); its Fèidh chapel kept with the graves after the gallery fall and the Board's removal of families (V).

492.name: Àth bheag
492.why: Shire seat on the east-coast ford.

493.name: Muileann gheal
493.why: 'A walled mill-camp' built in the Age of Strangers to crush coal.

496.name: Àth dhìreach
496.why: Founded by a mining crew under the human administration: the ford of the coal carts.

497.name: Seann Bhral
497.why: Walled harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site. Its port is kept: the town was moved 3 cells to the coast (see burg_moves.json).

499.name: Cill thais
499.why: Chapel village fortified with a citadel; its priests bless each ship of the fourth fleet.

500.name: Àth fhiadhaich
500.why: Paved ford whose shrine keepers take part in the capital's rites; the ford of the forty (II).

501.name: Cnoc gharbh
501.why: Quarry town whose camp huts were abandoned after the sickness and rebuilt by the Company for crews from the west (IV).

502.name: Muileann bhàn
502.why: Shire seat; citadel that held the Administration's weighing-house; the ancestor tradition 'has returned to the square'.

503.name: Baile dhubh
503.why: Former clerks' town living on the garrison.

504.name: Cnoc bheag
504.why: 'A fort with a citadel at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag' guarding the capital's south and the wood (group fort).

505.name: Muileann ruadh
505.why: Walled mill town whose walls went up when the inns fortified before the war.
